title: Vows to Saints are common; Thomas’s escape: the Saint-promise is vow-matter, the God-promise is the formal vow
source_text: XXVIII. Ad cultum quoque Sanctorum pertinere volunt Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae vota quae illis nuncupantur. In ea enim Ecclesia, valde usitatum est, nuncupare vota Sanctis, ac praesertim Beatae Virgini, quod licite fieri Doctores illius pertendunt. Verum cum Theologi votum ponant inter actus religionis soli Deo debitos, inde nascitur difficultas, quomodo ergo Sanctis vota fieri possint absque Idololatria. Ad hoc juxta doctrinam Thomae respondendum est, vota proprie Sanctis non fieri. Nam vota quae Sanctis fieri dicuntur includere duas promissiones: Unam quae fit Sanctis, & illam non esse formaliter votum, sed materiam voti: alteram vero quae Deo fit, & vere est votum. Nempe qui Virgini aliquid promittit, & tacite promittit Deo, se impleturum promissionem Virgini factam, & haec secunda promissio est vere votum.
pass_a_gloss: The Doctors of the Roman Church also will that vows which are vowed to them pertain to the cult of the Saints. For in that Church it is very customary to vow vows to the Saints, and especially to the Blessed Virgin, which her Doctors contend is done lawfully. But since Theologians place the vow among the acts of religion owed to God alone, thence arises the difficulty, how therefore vows can be made to the Saints without Idolatry. To this, according to the doctrine of Thomas, it is to be answered that vows are not properly made to the Saints. For vows which are said to be made to the Saints include two promises: One which is made to the Saints, and that is not formally a vow, but the matter of a vow: but the other which is made to God, and truly is a vow. Namely, he who promises something to the Virgin also tacitly promises to God that he will fulfill the promise made to the Virgin, and this second promise is truly a vow.
pass_b_english: Saint-vows (especially Marian) are everyday Roman praxis—yet vows are latria-acts.
Thomas’s patch: the Saint gets promise-matter; God alone gets the formal vow (tacitly guaranteeing fulfillment).

lemmas.gloss: vows which are vowed to them

choices.why: Only the Godward promise is the vow itself.
